newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Sampoerna hit hard after Moody's review.
newsitem.headline: Sampoerna hit hard after Moody's review.

text.p: Indonesian cigarette firm PT Hanjaya Mandala Sampoerna, which has bought into car maker Astra International, took a hit on Monday after Moody's said it may downgrade its long-term debt because of the purchase.

News that the rating agency had placed $200 million in notes issued by a Sampoerna subsidiary on review for a possible downgrade triggered a sharp fall in Sampoerna shares. The stock fell 1,325 rupiah, or 5.9 percent, to close at 21,125.
Brokers said Moody's news came as Sampoerna announced it had secured a fresh short-term bank facility of $400 million, and they were confused about why the company was seeking fresh funds.
On Saturday, the company announced it had obtained a $400 million loan but the terms were not disclosed. It said the money would be used for corporate development.

"Corporate development includes a number of aims such as ongoing expansion in domestic and overseas markets, to finance our inventory and also for acquisitions," company spokesman Jonathan Zax said on Monday.
But he declined to elaborate on what purchases were likely. "We are always investigating the possibilities of finding acquisitions or expansion in tobacco and related businesses," he added.

PT Sampoerna and president director Putera Sampoerna announced last week that the company had bought a 12.66 percent stake in Astra, Indonesia's largest automobile manufacturer, as an investment. Putera Sampoerna bought 9.81 percent of the company on his individual account while a Sampoerna subsidiary bought 2.85 percent.
Moody's said it had placed the Baa3 rating of Sampoerna International Finance Co B.V.'s $200 million notes on review following the acquisitions.

It said the moves "clearly indicate that Sampoerna intends to pursue a much more aggressive diversification strategy away from its original plan as well as its willingness to use a higher level of debt capacity for this purpose".

Moody's said the review would focus on the prospects for further investment by Sampoerna in Astra and, if the investment materialised, the method of financing, its impact on the predictability of the company's overall cash flow, and the magnitude of additional business and political risk incurred.
However Elaine Tedjojuwono, an analyst at Schroder Securities, said she still expected Sampoerna to outperform the market.

"For the time being we have no strong reason to downgrade Sampoerna as it has strong fundamentals," she said, but did not rule out a downgrade in the future. She added that the company's fresh loan had caused confusion and she was awaiting an explanation.

Zax said the loan had not been sought suddenly. "It is in line with our strategy ...," he said. He declined to comment on the possibility that the loan would be used to finance the purchase of additional shares in Astra.
He said the firm planned to hold an extraordinary general meeting on November 2, but the agenda was still unspecified.
